title: a coercing operator applied to a foreign value runs its `valueOf`, so unary `+` is a foreign call
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." One operator stands for the whole coercing family — prefix `+`/`-`/`~`, the loose comparisons, `+` with a string, a compound assignment, `instanceof`'s right operand, `in`'s left operand, a computed key and an element-access key — because they reach the rule through the same position predicate and not through separate branches. The deliberate exclusions are the operators that coerce nothing: `if (x)` and `x ? a : b` run ToBoolean, `x === 1` and `switch (x)` are strict, and none of those invokes user code.
